reading.title: Do we learn by listening?
reading.text: Many teachers still sort students into visual and auditory learners. The idea is attractive: some children, it is said, learn best when information is audible, others when it is shown. However, when psychologists carried out an audit of the research, they found little evidence for it. Students did not learn more when lessons matched their supposed style. This matters because schools spend money on training based on the theory. A better approach, researchers say, is to match the method to the content: music is learnt by ear, maps by eye, whatever the audience.
